question: The open public consultation on the Single Basic Act for Joint Undertakings (JUs) and thematic priorities for the European Partnerships portfolio in Horizon Europe 2028-2034 will inform the accompanying impact assessment. The questionnaire presents five ‘areas for improvement’ as findings the Commission ‘has identified’ and which ‘will have to be addressed by the future Treaty-based partnerships’.

Respondents are asked only whether they agree. The mandatory objectives (group 3) and measures (group 4) mirror those five areas one-to-one; a respondent who considers there to be no problem must still rate its causes and remedies. A footnote states the areas ‘do not necessarily pertain to all existing JUs, but are relevant to some JUs to varying extent’ – as worded, the propositions cannot be disagreed with.
Every open field is optional and additive, asking only for ‘other problems’, ‘other key factors’, ‘other objectives’ or ‘other measures ... not included above’. 1.
In which recorded field can a respondent state that one of the five areas is not a problem at all?
Will the impact assessment assess options that are not derived from these five areas?
Will disagreement with an area be reported separately from ‘cannot say’ in the quantative data reporting?
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (5.10.2026) The public consultation on the Single Basic Act for Joint Undertakings was published on the Have your say portal1 and will feed the preparation of the impact assessment (IA). It seeks views and evidence on how Treaty-based partnerships can be strengthened to boost EU competitiveness, mobilise investment and support the innovation-to-investment journey.

In question group 1, respondents may select the ’fully disagree’ where they think that the listed area does not constitute a problem. For the subsequent questions on contributing factors, objectives and measures, respondents may select ’Cannot say’ or ’I do not know’; in such cases, no - rating is recorded. The five areas reflect the Commission’s preliminary identification of possible areas for improvement.

Respondents can propose other possible areas for improvement by replying to question 6 of question group 1: ’Are there other problems to be considered in relation to Treaty-based partnerships that are not included above’. Moreover, the impact assessment will also reflect the results of the call for evidence.

Finally, the external study supporting the IA will conduct an evidence-based review of the identified problems and assess their magnitude. Thus, there is room for rescoping the problem areas based on the consultations and analyses. Fully disagree’ responses will be recorded and reported separately from ’Cannot say’ or ’I do not know’ responses in the quantitative analysis.
